title: Lessons in Hare Hunting: Inside Britain’s School Beagle Packs
content:
The private schools schooling children in a masterclass of wildlife criminality.




Recently we revealed the 

full footage of the Stowe School Beagles

 during what school headteacher, Dr Anthony Wallersteiner, describes as a 

“huge variety of activities”

 available to pupils, including 

“field games…beagling”

.




Kennedy giving direction to the pupils




The school’s Games Coach, Phillip Kennedy, was in the fields surrounding Crockwell Farm, alongside school pupils, ‘coaching’ them as the Stowe School Beagles hunted a hare.




The school lesson ended with a dead hare and a criminal conviction for its Games Coach.




The now-deleted reference to Kennedy’s role at the Stowe School.




Kennedy pleaded guilty to hunting a wild mammal with dogs after drone footage captured his pack chasing the hare, first through the farmyard and then across open fields before catching and killing her against a fence. 

Police said

 that Kennedy knew allowing his dogs to chase and kill the hare was cruel and illegal.




Just as importantly, the footage shone a spotlight on something that has gone on behind the closed doors of some of Britain’s most prestigious private schools: children being introduced to illegal hunting, more than twenty years after hunting wild mammals with dogs was banned.

title: Eggesford in the Dock: Huntsman Convicted of Illegal Hunting
content:
Eggesford Hunt huntsman Jason Marles has been convicted of illegally hunting a fox with hounds following an incident captured on drone footage during the hunt’s Boxing Day meet in December 2025.




Jason Marles, huntsman of the Eggesford Hunt.




Marles, 44, pleaded guilty to hunting a wild mammal with dogs at Pudson Farm, near Okehampton, when he appeared before Exeter Magistrates’ Court on 23 September 2026.




His conviction followed footage recorded by Devon County Hunt Saboteurs which showed a fox being bolted from an area of rubble before being pursued by hounds. Hunt saboteurs positioned on a farm track nearby were in position to stop the hounds from chasing the fox, and they confirmed that the fox managed to evade capture.




The footage shows Marles standing beside the area where the fox had taken refuge, close to a cattle barn. Two men with spades are moving rubble and digging at the site, while a child, who had dismounted from their pony, also watches what is happening.




Huntsman Jason Marles looks on as landowner Lloyd Heard and terrier-man Tom Bounsall dig and remove the rubble protecting the hunted fox. Image credit: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs.




Devon County Hunt Sabs identify the two men digging as Eggesford terrier man Tom Bounsall and landowner Lloyd Heard.

author: hsa_oryx
title: MENDIP FARMERS HUNT TO FACE TRIAL OVER HUNTED FOX
content:
Three people associated with the Mendip Farmers Hunt have pleaded not guilty to hunting a wild mammal with dogs.




Emma Clothier, Charlie Thomas and Bill Payne appeared at Taunton Deane Magistrates’ Court on 15 September 2026. All three pleaded not guilty and are due to face trial on 15 September 2027.




Emma Clothier (l) Charlie Thomas (c) and Bill Payne (r) . 

Image Credit Mendip Hunt Sabs.




The case relates to events on 17th January 2026, when the Mendip Farmers Hunt met at their kennels in Priddy, Somerset.




Mendip Hunt Sabs were with the hunt throughout the day and documented the day’s events, including from the air using a drone. After the meet, sabs reviewed the footage they had recorded.




The footage shows hounds working inside thick bramble for several minutes before a fox breaks cover. A group of hunters can be seen on an adjoining track, including two people on horseback and a person on foot, while other mounted riders can be seen around the bramble.




The person on foot is standing only a short distance from where the fox emerges and can be seen pointing in the direction in which the fox runs.




The fox breaks cover from the thick bramble. 

Image Credit Mendip Hunt Sabs.




The hounds immediately give chase.




Within approximately a minute, the hounds catch the fox. The drone records the pack converging on the animal and the fox being killed.

title: Quantock Hunt Members Charged
content:
At long last, charges have been issued against members of a stag hunt. 




Huntsman Martin Watts. Image Credit Mendip Hunt Sabs




Avon and Somerset Police have charged Quantock Staghounds hunt master Chris Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts with illegally hunting a wild mammal with dogs in relation to an incident on March 16, 2026.




Watts faces a further charge relating to a separate incident on April 23, 2026.




Both men are to appear in Taunton Magistrates’ Court on October 22, 2026 to answer the charges.




Hunt master Chris Gibbons. Image credit North Dorset Hunt Saboteurs




The charges follow what was, for a stag hunt, an ordinary day in March, when hunt saboteurs from Mendip Hunts Sabs and North Dorset Hunt Sabs were in attendance and recorded events as they unfolded.




The stag was first seen by sabs at around noon

. It would be almost six o’clock before the day was over and the stag was dead.




For more than five hours sabs documented the pursuit as the animal repeatedly fled. Quads, hunters on horseback, hounds and even motorbikes were involved as the stag attempted to escape.




It is difficult to comprehend what five hours of pursuit actually means for the animal. Deer are not endurance runners, prolonged exertion can cause severe physiological stress and overheating, and exhausted deer often enter rivers or streams during or following a pursuit.

title: Devon And Somerset Staghounds Recreate The Horror Of The Barle Stag
content:
Thirty-two years on from the controversy of the Barle stag, the excuses may have changed, but for the hunted stag the suffering is horribly familiar.




More than three decades have passed since the death of the Barle stag became one of the most notorious episodes associated with stag hunting on Exmoor. Yet for those who witnessed what happened on Saturday 12th September 2026, the events along the River Barle carried disturbing echoes of the past – a past that, sadly, does not seem so very different from the present.




On Saturday, this magnificent stag was found quickly in the boggy woodland below Twitchen, and from there the pursuit began.




The stag was described as “a very fine up and coming stag” by a deer expert from Wildlife Guardian




A sab from North Dorset Hunt Saboteurs struggled to keep pace as the stag was chased across Molland Common and West Anstey Common. The stag crossed the road just moments before sabs arrived.




From there, the stag continued towards the River Barle at Mountsey Castle. It was there that sabs saw him bursting across a track in front of point riders and a quad bike before heading down and into the river.
